sections.h2: Where is Barnstable and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
Barnstable is a town on Cape Cod and the county seat of Barnstable County. It is the largest community on the Cape by both land area and population, and it sits roughly 70 miles southeast of Boston.

The town covers about 76 square miles, and a little over a fifth of that is water. Cape Cod Bay forms the northern edge and Nantucket Sound the southern edge. Sandwich and Mashpee border Barnstable on the west, and Yarmouth borders it on the east.

Barnstable is a group of villages that have no legal boundaries of their own, and these seven are the ones most often listed:

  • Barnstable village, which includes Cummaquid
  • Centerville
  • Cotuit
  • Hyannis, which includes Hyannis Port and West Hyannisport
  • Marstons Mills
  • Osterville
  • West Barnstable

The Sandy Neck dunes run along Barnstable Harbor in the north. Pines and oaks surround Wequaquet Lake in the middle of town. Most residents live in the south, and many of them live near the beaches of Centerville and Hyannis Harbors. Hyannis is the biggest village.

sections.h2: What is the short history of Barnstable?
sections.html:
English settlers founded Barnstable in 1638, and it was incorporated in 1639 as one of the early towns of Plymouth Colony. It was named after Barnstaple in Devon, England.

Farming, fishing and salt works came first. By the end of the 1800s the town harbored hundreds of ships, and the railroad arrived in 1854. Summer visitors followed, and the Kennedy family compound in Hyannis Port is the best known result of that history.

In 1989 the town rewrote its charter and moved from selectmen and town meeting to a council and town manager system. Barnstable is one of thirteen Massachusetts municipalities that hold a city form of government but keep "the town of" in their official name. For a seller, the practical point is that you deal with Town Hall in Hyannis, not a city hall, even though the government is council based.

sections.h2: What does the Barnstable economy run on?
sections.html:
Hyannis acts as the commercial center of Cape Cod, and that gives Barnstable a mix of tourism, health care, transportation and education jobs.

  • Cape Cod Hospital is in Hyannis and serves the central Cape.
  • Barnstable Municipal Airport is the regional hub for flights between the Cape and the islands, and Cape Air is headquartered in town.
  • The main ferry lines to Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard leave from Hyannis.
  • Cape Cod Community College is based in Barnstable.
  • The county courthouse and the offices of the Cape and Islands District Attorney are here because Barnstable is the county seat.

Barnstable also has the largest public school enrollment on the Cape, with more than 5,000 students according to Wikipedia's profile of the town.

sections.h2: How does Cape Cod weather affect a Barnstable house?
sections.html:
Barnstable has a humid continental climate, with an average seasonal snowfall of about 30 inches from November through April. February is typically the snowiest month, and it lines up with the peak of nor'easter activity.

The USDA places the town in plant hardiness zone 7a. With snow and nor'easters in the picture, the roof and the heating system are the items a buyer's inspector is likely to look at first.

A cash buyer does not need those repairs finished. If a nor'easter has already damaged a roof or a deck, the house can still be sold as it stands.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and ferries shape buyer demand in Barnstable?
sections.html:
Route 6 is a four lane freeway across Barnstable, and Route 28 runs east and west through town as well. Routes 6A, 132 and 149 are the other main roads, and Routes 132 and 149 lie entirely inside the town.

Rail is limited. The CapeFlyer runs on weekends between Memorial Day and Labor Day. The nearest MBTA commuter rail stations with year round service are Middleborough and Kingston, so a commute to Boston is mostly a drive. Logan Airport is the nearest national and international airport, while Barnstable Municipal Airport handles regional flights.

sections.h2: When are Barnstable property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Barnstable bills real estate tax in four quarterly payments each fiscal year. For fiscal 2027, the Treasurer/Collector lists these dates:

BillDue date
First quarter (preliminary bill)August 3, 2026
Second quarter (preliminary bill)November 2, 2026
Third quarter (actual bill)February 1, 2027
Fourth quarter (actual bill)May 3, 2027

Preliminary bills were mailed by July 1, 2026, and actual bills are to be mailed by December 31, 2026. The Collector also bills motor vehicle and boat excise, sewer usage, and betterments for roads, water, sewer and septic. A betterment is a charge tied to the property, so mention any you know of to your closing attorney.

The Collector's page carries a municipal lien certificate request form. Ask your closing attorney whether one is needed for your sale. The Tax Collections line is 508-862-4054, and Town Hall is at 367 Main Street in Hyannis.

If you think your assessment is too high, an abatement application goes to the assessors. In towns that bill quarterly, that application is generally due February 1, and the Appellate Tax Board hears appeals after that.

sections.h2: Does a Barnstable house on septic need a Title 5 inspection before a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, in most cases. Under the state's Title 5 rules, a septic system generally has to be inspected within two years before a sale, or within six months after it if weather prevents an inspection beforehand. The Collector's page shows that Barnstable bills for sewer and for septic betterments, so some addresses are on sewer and some are not. Check which applies to yours.

  • Only MassDEP approved inspectors can do the inspection, and the report goes on the state form within 30 days.
  • The buyer must receive a copy of the report.
  • A passing inspection is generally good for two years. It is good for three years if the system is pumped every year and the records are in the report.
  • A conditional pass covers items like a cracked tank or a broken pipe, but cesspools and soil absorption systems cannot be repaired under a conditional pass.
  • A failed system must be upgraded within two years unless the Board of Health agrees to another schedule.

Transfers between spouses, parents and children, or full siblings are exempt, as are some trust and estate planning transfers. Buyers can also sign a binding agreement with the Board of Health to upgrade or connect to sewer within two years.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Barnstable County?
sections.html:
Massachusetts charges a deed excise tax when a deed is recorded, and the statute sets a lower rate for Barnstable County than for the rest of the state. The statutory text gives $1.50 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it in Barnstable County.

Sale priceDeed excise at $1.50 per $500
$400,000$1,200
$600,000$1,800
$900,000$2,700

Recording fees are set separately by the registry, so ask your closing attorney for the current figure.

sections.h2: What must be done before closing a Barnstable sale?
sections.html:
Three items come up in nearly every Massachusetts sale of a one or two family home.

  • Smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. You need a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing your alarms meet the rules for a sale. Call the department as soon as you have a closing date, and expect a fee. Battery alarms older than ten years must be replaced with sealed ten year photoelectric alarms.
  • An attorney. Massachusetts treats real estate closings as legal work. A Massachusetts court decision describes closings as requiring an attorney's substantive participation on behalf of the lender.
  • Title system. Most properties are recorded land filed at the Registry of Deeds. A smaller share is registered land with a Land Court certificate of title.

State rules also stop sellers of certain residential properties from conditioning an offer on a buyer waiving a home inspection.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Barnstable usually run into?
sections.html:
The town spans seven villages with different surroundings, from harbor streets in Hyannis to the wooded interior near Wequaquet Lake. A house in Cotuit and a house in West Barnstable can have very different sewer, water and tax situations, so confirm the details with the Treasurer/Collector and the Board of Health rather than assuming.

If the house needs septic work, has a betterment on it, or has been vacant through a Cape winter, a direct sale can save you the repair bills and the wait for an inspector. We buy Barnstable houses as they are.

faqs.q: Is Barnstable a town or a city?
faqs.a: Both. Barnstable keeps the name Town of Barnstable but has run under a council and town manager charter since 1989, and it is one of thirteen Massachusetts municipalities with a city form of government that kept the town name.

faqs.q: How many villages are in Barnstable?
faqs.a: Seven are commonly listed: Barnstable, Centerville, Cotuit, Hyannis, Marstons Mills, Osterville and West Barnstable. They have no legal boundaries, and some lists count as many as eleven.

faqs.q: When is the next Barnstable property tax payment due?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2027 the remaining dates are February 1, 2027 for the third quarter and May 3, 2027 for the fourth. Check your actual bill, since the Treasurer/Collector sets the schedule each year.

faqs.q: Do I need a septic inspection to sell my Barnstable house?
faqs.a: Usually yes if the home has a septic system. Title 5 calls for an inspection within two years before the sale, or within six months after if weather blocks it, unless an exemption such as a family transfer applies.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax in Barnstable County?
faqs.a: The statute sets $1.50 for each $500 of the sale price or fraction of it in Barnstable County. On a $600,000 sale that comes to $1,800.
